children: BNP Paribas cut its earnings estimate for BWX Technologies
ahead of the nuclear technology and defense contractor’s Sept. 29 investor day. The bank lowered those estimates by roughly 3% to 4%, leaving its forecasts close to the Wall Street consensus.
Senior analyst Matthew Akers maintained the firm’s rating on BWXT
while adjusting earnings estimates to reflect higher expected margins in the company’s defense operations, lower margins in its commercial business and changes to below-the-line items.
The firm also cut its price target to $165 from $190, citing lower valuation multiples across the defense and nuclear sectors. The new target represents about 16% upside from BWXT’s
Sept. 23 closing price of $141.80.
The price-target reduction appears to be primarily a valuation call rather than a significant change in BNP Paribas’ view of BWXT’s

underlying business. The firm sees potential for margin improvement in Government Operations and longer-term growth from the commercial nuclear market. The Sept. 29 investor day could provide investors with new medium-term financial targets and additional details about potential nuclear reactor orders that could become more meaningful toward the end of the decade.
Government margins in focus
BNP Paribas expects Government Operations to offer an opportunity for margin expansion as pressures associated with older naval reactor contracts and the ramp-up of newer programs diminish.
Those programs include High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium Deconversion and Preparation, or HDPU, Defense Fuels and development reactors including Janus, Pele and Draco.

The firm models Government Operations margins of about 21% in 2027, an increase of roughly 40 basis points from the prior year. That contrasts with consensus expectations for a year-over-year decline.

BNP Paribas also estimates increased equity income could contribute the equivalent of another 150 to 200 basis points compared with pre-pandemic levels, when adjusted Government Operations margins exceeded 20%.
Commercial nuclear could provide longer-term upside
On the commercial side, BNP Paribas expects efficiency improvements, higher volumes and the integration of Kinectrics to support growth and profitability.
Investors also will be listening for information about possible new-build orders involving Westinghouse or GE Vernova. Such awards could lift BWXT’s
longer-term growth outlook, although BNP Paribas expects relatively little contribution in 2027 and sees greater potential by 2030.
The analyst noted that BWXT
exceeded targets presented at its previous investor day in 2024, potentially giving management room to establish another set of achievable medium-term goals.
Medical exit sharpens strategy

BNP Paribas also views BWXT’s decision to divest its medical business favorably. The firm doesn’t anticipate significant additional portfolio pruning but expects management to explain how the divestiture better aligns the company with its longer-term strategy.
The analyst expects capital allocation to emphasize organic investment and acquisitions while preserving balance-sheet flexibility and returning capital to shareholders.
